clue.text: Pinafore, typically, in which you'll find entertainer works

parts.note: a comic is a comedian, a stage entertainer
opera is the Latin plural of opus, so it means works

explanation.surface: Someone describes where an entertainer's works are to be found in a pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan show; 'Pinafore' at the start looks like an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Pinafore is a light, humorous stage work set to music, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Mug shots cops use, maybe, to arrest unqualified driver

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold within, so one piece is held inside the other
maybe suggests the letters of the words cops use could be arranged another way

parts.note: a learner driver displays an L plate

explanation.surface: Police use photographs of a suspect after arresting a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrest' puts L inside COSEUPS, the anagram of COPS USE signalled by 'maybe'. 'Mug' is slang for face.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is slang for a face, and photographs taken at very close range of a face are this kind of shot.

clue.text: New book, the first of its kind

definitions.text: New book, the first of its kind

parts.words: New book, the first of its kind
parts.note: reads as a novel that founds a genre, but means the opening book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises a groundbreaking new publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' points to the New Testament, whose first book is the Gospel of this evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of this apostle opens the New Testament, so it is that collection's first book.

clue.text: Fear that's never revealed openly?

parts.note: reads as a secret dread, but means a dread felt only in enclosed spaces, never in the open

explanation.surface: Someone hides an anxiety they never admit in public.
explanation.definitionFit: This phobia is dread of confined spaces, so it shows itself only when shut in, not out in the open.

clue.text: Smoother specimen in the arboretum?

parts.note: a plane is a carpenter's smoothing tool, and its namesake grows among the trees of an arboretum

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a particularly sleek specimen in a tree collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A plane is the woodworker's tool that smooths timber, and a tree of the same name stands in the arboretum.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane and its relatives are common trees grown in parks and arboreta.

clue.text: Reject first of partners in dance

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the dance word

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word partners

explanation.surface: A dancer turns down the first partner who asks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P, picked by 'first of' from 'partners', inside REEL, a Scottish folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject is to drive back or refuse, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: It spelled the end for one Roman and several Greeks

definitions.text: It spelled the end for one Roman and several Greeks

parts.words: It spelled the end for one Roman and several Greeks
parts.note: the day in March fatal to Caesar, and the ending spelt in Greek names such as ... and ...

explanation.surface: A historian recalls a date that doomed a Roman and some Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was killed on the Ides of March; 'spelled the end' also means the letters that end Greek names like Euripides, Aristides and Thucydides.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth day of March in the Roman calendar was Caesar's death day, and the same letters close many Greek names.

clue.text: Detective's failure to identify cashier

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with 's added
a miss is a failure to hit

explanation.surface: A police officer fails to pick out a bank cashier in a line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' looks like a bank clerk, but here it is the verb meaning to sack someone, especially from the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier someone is to sack them from service, especially from the military.

clue.text: Fuse is relatively ancient

parts.note: is shortens to 's, giving S
relatively ancient means more aged than something else

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a fuse in the house is fairly old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuse' is the verb, to join metal by melting.
explanation.definitionFit: To join metal parts with a molten alloy is to weld or melt them together.

clue.text: Smooth-bore firear?

parts.note: the word firearm with its last letter cut off pictures a gun whose barrel has been cut short

explanation.surface: A gun catalogue lists a smooth-bore weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firear' is 'firearm' with its end removed, just as this weapon has had its barrel cut down; the printed word is deliberate, not a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bore gun whose barrel has been shortened is the weapon pictured by a truncated word for gun.

clue.text: Very large body of soldiers seen around island's old port

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

indicators.note: seen around means the soldiers' letters are wrapped round the island letter

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Big troop formations surround an island's ancient harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts TA round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour town of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Shock overwhelming one getting in painter's estimate

indicators.note: overwhelming means covering over, so the shock word surrounds the rest

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: getting in means the numeral goes inside the painter's letters

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter, with 's added
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An art valuer is shocked by a painter's price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' and 'overwhelming' stack two containers: the numeral goes in first, then the shock word wraps it all. RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a valuation or assessment of worth.

clue.text: Tea container from posh service

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tea vessel comes from an upmarket china set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a tea service, but it is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal vessel with a tap is used to keep tea hot for serving many people.

clue.text: Atmosphere in Dorset hospital

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words Dorset hospital

explanation.surface: Someone praises the atmosphere of a county hospital in Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic spirit or culture of a place or group is its character, a sense of atmosphere.

clue.text: Say part of poem about insect and flower

parts.note: eg (for example) can stand for say

indicators.note: about means the poem piece wraps round the insect

parts.note: a line is part of a poem
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A verse about an insect and a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual signal for eg; 'about' wraps the line round the insect. Eglantine is sweetbriar.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweetbriar, a wild rose.

clue.text: Business with electric toaster?

parts.note: reads as an appliance needing electricity, but describes a morning meal where business is done

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a toaster at breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electric' suggests a toaster on the mains, but power also means influence, and executives do business over this kind of meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Executives hold early working meetings over a morning meal, which has this name.

clue.text: White gypsum altar base, elaborately carved

indicators.note: something carved elaborately is reshaped, so the letters of altar base are reworked

explanation.surface: A church altar's base is ornately sculpted in white stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborately carved' rearranges ALTAR BASE.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft white stone is a fine-grained form of gypsum used for carving.

clue.text: Wanton ladies to stray?

indicators.note: wanton means unruly or undisciplined, so the letters of ladies to run wild

explanation.surface: Loose women are tempted to wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanton' rearranges LADIES TO. 'stray' is the adjective, as in a stray case: one apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray instance is a lone or solitary one, standing apart from others.

clue.text: Over-ornate descriptions of voyages on the wine-dark sea?

definitions.meaning: Homer's sea is 'wine-dark', a rich red-purple colour, and voyages are journeys by sea

explanation.surface: A critic complains about flowery accounts of Homeric sea voyages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wine-dark sea' is Homer's phrase; read literally, journeys across a purple sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwritten, showy prose is known by a phrase from Horace, and sea journeys through purple water fit the same words.

clue.text: Prince, one entertained by thug playing piano

indicators.note: entertained by means held inside, as a guest inside a host's house
playing means the letters of thug are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prince is hosted by a thug who plays the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts PRI inside UGHT, the anagram of THUG signalled by 'playing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument with its strings set vertically in a tall case is a common household type of piano.

clue.text: Defence used after agent's released?

parts.note: reads as protection once a spy is freed, but means protection worn once a chemical agent is let loose

explanation.surface: Precautions are taken once a spy is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' suggests a secret agent, but it is a chemical agent such as nerve gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A face covering with a filter protects the wearer from poisonous chemical weapons.

clue.text: Pub served up sole in carbolic acid

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the word for sole is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sole means only, lone

explanation.surface: A pub serves fish in a disinfectant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns LONE upwards to ENOL. 'sole' looks like the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic acid is the old name for the simplest aromatic alcohol, used as a disinfectant.

clue.text: Instrument played on March I by leading

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of on March I are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: A means first-class or top, as in A-list

explanation.surface: An instrument is played on the first of March by the lead performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ON MARCH I; 'by' just places A beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a small wind instrument played by blowing across reeds.

clue.text: Showing little competence in English exercises

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone is poor at English drills.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, was the old school name for gym exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill.

clue.text: Bird seen flying in Seoul

indicators.note: flying means the letters of Seoul are scattered in flight into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted in flight over the South Korean capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges SEOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousel is an old name for the blackbird and related thrushes.

clue.text: Take examination in Lettish retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the run is read in reverse
in means the letters lie inside the word Lettish

explanation.surface: Someone takes an exam in the Latvian language.
explanation.walkthrough: Lettish is an old name for Latvian. 'in' finds TIS inside it and 'retrospectively' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an exam is to take it.

clue.text: Careless, literally, about information provided

annotationWithheld.why: 'Careless, literally, about information provided' (9) for NEGLIGENT: LI(GEN)T gives LIGENT but no clue word supplies NEG (only 'about' could reverse GEN, which is already used), and no reprint or blog was found

clue.text: Greek behind corrupt practices?

parts.note: aft means at the back, behind

explanation.surface: A Greek is blamed for corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Graft is bribery and corruption, especially in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is political corruption, gaining money or advantage by dishonest dealings.

clue.text: Deceased's silverware quietly abstracted

definitions.note: the definition reads as 'deceased is', the 's being 'is'

indicators.note: abstracted means taken away, so the quiet letter is stolen from the silverware word

parts.note: plate is silver or gold tableware
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A dead person's silver has been quietly stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstracted' removes P from PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The late someone is a person who has died recently.

clue.text: Army in shivering ranks appearing before King Edward with nothing on

indicators.note: in means the army letters go inside the shaken ranks
shivering means trembling, so the letters of ranks shake into a new order

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Soldiers shiver in the ranks before the king, wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' makes SRKNA from the ranks; 'appearing before' just orders the charade. 'with nothing on' looks like part of the scene of cold soldiers, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked means completely nude, without a stitch of clothing.
